title: Review: Doppler effect; Expanding universe and cosmology; Progressive waves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; A03-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; W01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; A03-2#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: A03-2#N.8, W01-1#N.1, W01-uk1#N.5, W11-1#N.13a, A03-2#N.7, W01-1#N.15, W01-uk1#N.3, W11-1#N.9, A03-2#N.3, W01-uk1#N.10, W11-1#N.6. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position.

items.label: Recession speed
items.clue: How fast a galaxy is moving away from us, found from its red shift.

items.label: In phase
items.clue: Relation between points one wavelength apart, which move exactly together.

items.label: Hubble's law
items.clue: Finding that a distant galaxy twice as far away is moving away twice as fast.

questions.stem: Galaxy P is 2.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 5.2 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Galaxy Q is 6.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 1.56 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Assuming each has always moved at its present speed, how long ago was each at our position? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

options.text: P 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago, Q 3.7 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they set off at different times.
Both 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Both 3.8 × 10¹⁷ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Never: the further galaxy moves faster, so the two can never have been together.

questions.explanation: Distance ÷ speed = 3.8 × 10¹⁷ s for both, which is 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years. Speed ∝ distance gives every galaxy the same time.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker plays a steady note to a listener 5 m away in a room with still air. Which of the following travels from the loudspeaker to the listener?

options.text: Energy, passed along by air molecules that vibrate about fixed positions
Air molecules, pushed across the room from the loudspeaker to the ear
Sound particles, which the loudspeaker gives off and the air carries
An electromagnetic signal, which needs no air to carry it across

questions.stem: Two displacement–time graphs, P and Q, show the oscillations of two points on a wave. Both have a period of 6.0 ms. Each crest of Q comes 1.0 ms after the matching crest of P. What is the phase difference between P and Q?

A calcium absorption line has a wavelength of 393.4 nm in the laboratory. In the spectrum of a distant galaxy the same line is at 401.3 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the galaxy's velocity relative to Earth?
questions.explanation: Δλ = 7.9 nm; v = c × 7.9/393.4 = 6.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Longer wavelength → receding.

questions.stem: A measured value of the Hubble constant is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. What is the estimated age of the universe? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

A vibrator sends waves along a stretched string at constant tension. At 25 Hz the wavelength is 0.80 m. The frequency is raised to 100 Hz. What is the new wavelength, and how long does a wave now take to travel 4.0 m along the string?
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 25 × 0.80 = 20 m s⁻¹, unchanged. New λ = 20/100 = 0.20 m; time = 4.0/20 = 0.20 s, the same as before.

questions.stem: Two points on a progressive wave of wavelength 1.2 m are 0.40 m apart along the direction of travel. What is the phase difference between their oscillations?
questions.explanation: Right. Δx/λ = 0.40/1.2 = ⅓ cycle, and ⅓ × 2π = 2π/3 rad (120°).

questions.stem: Predict first. Every absorption line in the spectrum of a star in our galaxy is at a slightly longer wavelength than the same line measured in the laboratory. What does this show about the star?

options.text: It is a cool, red-looking star.
It is moving away from Earth.
It is a very long way from Earth.

questions.stem: A galaxy at a distance of 1.2 × 10²⁴ m recedes from the Earth at 2800 km s⁻¹. What value of the Hubble constant does this give?
questions.explanation: H₀ = speed ÷ distance = 2.8 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ ÷ 1.2 × 10²⁴ m = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker emits a steady 500 Hz note. Two microphones are placed on a straight line from the loudspeaker, 0.17 m apart. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How do the oscillations detected by the two microphones compare?

options.text: They are in antiphase, π rad apart.
They are a quarter of a cycle, π/2 rad, apart.
They are in phase, as the note has one frequency.
They are an eighth of a cycle, π/4 rad, apart.

questions.stem: A spectral line of hydrogen has a wavelength of 656.3 nm when measured in the laboratory. A galaxy is moving directly away from Earth at 3.00 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. At what wavelength is this line observed in the spectrum of the galaxy?
